locked_story.headline: A machine-learning model trained on 2019 lightning and weather projects Alaska could see 116% to 594% more ground-striking lightning by 2100, in a state where lightning starts most of the wildfire acreage (Earth's Future, Krause et al., AGU release November 24th)
locked_story.note: Surfaced 2026-11-26 as a runner-up, verified in window today (AGU release and EurekAlert November 24th, NatureWorldNews November 25th). ML is load-bearing: the projection is the model. Honest tension: one training year asked about the 2090s, a 2x to 7x range on a low base. dedupe FRESH.

rungs.note: 3 researchers (fresh news sweep, science lead deep dig, policy/infrastructure/defense), about 47 WebSearch calls, many uncapped WebFetches. All three called it a slow Thanksgiving week.

Covered in round one: ADN, Alaska Public, Alaska Beacon (partly 403), KTOO, Alaska's News Source, News-Miner, Must Read Alaska, UAF, UAA, KYUK, KDLL, KUCB, KTNA, Alaska Business, Alaska Native News, Arctic Today, DVIDS indexes read.

Runner-up leads from runs/2026-11-24 to 11-26 candidates.json re-verified: lightning (strong), glacier lakes (usable), avalanche roads (no ML), bowhead fiber (no ML in sources), USGS polar bears (October 8th, out of window), Bering Strait ice forecast (model type unverified).
